body.p: Please AMEND the claims as follows:

br.br:
1-20. (Cancelled)
219
21. (Currently Amended) A method of providing a continuity of care for a patient having or at risk of developing pressure ulcers (PU) during transfer from a first care setting to a second care setting, the method comprising the steps of:
identifying a current PU intervention of level-K received by the patient at the first care setting, wherein the current PU intervention of level-K is provided in a transfer record;
making a plurality of Sub-Epidermal Moisture (SEM) measurements at a body location on the patient at the second care setting, calculating a delta value by a difference between two of the plurality of SEM measurements, determining whether the delta value exceeds a threshold, continuing to administer the current PU intervention if the delta value does not exceed the threshold, and
administering a new PU intervention of level-N if the delta value exceeds the threshold, where N has a value greater than K.
22. (Cancelled)
23. (Currently Amended) The method of claim [[22]] 2_L wherein the transfer record further comprises delta values calculated from a portion of the plurality of SEM scans of the patient taken at different times while in the first care setting.
24. (Currently Amended) The method of claim [[22]] 2 _, wherein the transfer record further comprises results obtained from at least one of assessments selected from the group consisting of a risk assessment of the patient, a visual skin assessment of at least one body location of the patient, and an image of the at least one body location.
25. (Currently Amended) The method of claim [[22]] 21, wherein the transfer record further comprises results obtained from performing a first SEM scan of at least one body location of the patient while in the first care setting, wherein the first SEM scan comprises a plurality of measurements of an SEM value at the body location and calculation of a first delta value from the plurality of SEM values, and wherein said transfer record is stored on a database.
26. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 25, wherein:
the transfer record further comprises a patient identifier and a date and a time when said first SEM scan was performed.
27. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 21, further comprising continuing to make a plurality of SEM measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-K if the delta value does not exceed the threshold, and making a plurality of SEM measurements at a pre-determined frequency corresponding to level-N if the delta value exceeds the threshold.
28. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 21, wherein said delta value is calculated by a difference between a maximum SEM measurement and a minimum SEM measurement selected from the plurality of SEM measurements.
29. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 26, further comprising the steps of:
performing a second SEM scan of the body location of the patient in the second care setting to obtain a second plurality of SEM measurements, calculating a second delta value, creating a second data record that comprises the patient identifier, the second delta value, and a second date and time when the second SEM scan was performed, and
reporting the second data record to the database.
30. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 29, wherein said second delta value is calculated by a difference between a maximum SEM measurement and a minimum SEM measurement selected from the second plurality of SEM measurements.
31. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 29, further comprising the step of:
querying the database for the delta value and the second delta value of the at least one body location of the patient in the transfer record and the second data record respectively to form retrieved delta values.
32. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 31, further comprising the steps of:
formatting the retrieved delta values in date and time order, and
displaying the formatted delta values.
33. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 29, further comprising the steps of:
creating an additional data record that comprises the patient identifier, a data element, and a date/time associated with the data element, wherein the data element comprises one or more of a nutritional information, an implemented intervention, a risk assessment, a visual skin assessment, a care plan, a doctor's note, an event, a vital sign, a body weight, and a lab result, and
reporting the additional data record to the database.
34. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 32, wherein the formatted delta values are displayed in the form of a curve.
35. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 32, further comprising the step of analyzing the retrieved delta values to determine one or more of a slope, an acceleration, a curve shape and associated characteristics, and a time-to-intercept of a selected threshold value.
36. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 35, wherein the acceleration is determined by the rate of change of the slope of the curve.
37. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 29, further comprising the steps of:
performing a third SEM scan of the at least one body location of the patient in the second care setting to obtain a third plurality of SEM measurements, calculating a third delta value, creating a third data record that comprises the patient identifier, the third delta value, and
a third date and time when the third SEM scan was performed, and
reporting the third data record to a database.
38. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 37, wherein said third delta value is calculated by a difference between a maximum SEM measurement and a minimum SEM measurement selected from the third plurality of SEM measurements.
39. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 37, further comprising the step of querying the database to retrieve the delta values observed over time for a particular patient across multiple care settings and various episodes of care.
40. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 21, wherein a level-0 PU intervention is selected from the group consisting of providing good nutrition, standard mattress, turning every 24 hours, and a combination thereof.
41. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 21, wherein a level-1 PU intervention is providing a heel boot to the patient.
42. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 21, wherein a level-2 PU intervention is changing the patient's support surface.
43. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 21, wherein a level-3 PU intervention is applying dressing to the back or sides of patient's heel.
44. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 21, wherein a level-4 PU intervention is changing the patient's sheet cover to a low-friction sheet cover.
45. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 21, wherein a level-5 PU intervention is providing a low-friction padded mattress surface for the patient's lower leg.
46. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 21, wherein a level-6 PU intervention is turning the patient at a shorter interval than currently provided for.
47. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 21, wherein a level-7 PU intervention is applying a barrier cream to the patient's heel.
48. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 21, wherein a level-8 PU intervention is applying a neuro-muscular stimulation to the patient's heel.
49. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 21, wherein a level-9 PU intervention is applying a topical cream to the patient's heel to enhance perfusion.
50. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 21, wherein a level-10 PU intervention is providing a silicon pad for the patient's lower leg.
